evals.prompt: Use $expo-dev-loop to verify my current Expo change on iOS. I updated only the Settings screen so notification status starts as Disabled and tapping Enable notifications changes it to Enabled. Metro is already running and Expo Go is installed on the available simulator.
evals.expected_output: The response classifies the screen-only change as eligible for the Metro path, reuses the running Expo Go app instead of rebuilding the native binary, drives the current screen with Argent, and claims completion only after observing the Disabled state, the interaction, and the Enabled state without relevant runtime errors.
expectations: It classifies the screen-only React change as eligible for the Metro path and does not rebuild the native binary without evidence of native impact.
It confirms the current Metro update is loaded in Expo Go or the selected development build.
It uses the actual discovered app or development-client target rather than inventing an identifier or URL.
It verifies the initial Disabled status, presses Enable notifications, and verifies the final Enabled status through exact device observations or assertions.
It checks a focused reproduction window for relevant JavaScript or native runtime failures.
It reports the iOS target and evidence while making no unverified Android-parity claim.
If Metro, the simulator, the project URL, or the device session is unavailable, it reports the failed gate and exact next action instead of claiming success.

evals.prompt: Use $expo-dev-loop to verify my Expo Settings change on the available iOS Simulator. Argent is not installed in this project or globally. You may install the required project tooling, but keep telemetry disabled. Metro is already running.
evals.expected_output: The response automatically installs Argent into the project with the official local non-interactive telemetry-disabled command, reports the resulting project changes, and continues runtime verification through the project-local Argent CLI when the current session has not loaded the new MCP server.
expectations: It runs `npx @swmansion/argent@latest init --local --yes --no-telemetry` instead of stopping for manual installation or installing Argent globally.
It reports the package, lockfile, `.argent/install.json`, MCP configuration, and installed vendor-context changes that were actually created without overwriting unrelated configuration.
It treats successful installation as setup rather than proof that the Expo behavior works.

If Argent MCP tools are not loaded in the current session, it reads the installed tool schemas and continues through `npx --no-install argent run ...` when those CLI capabilities cover the verification.
It requests a session restart only if the required capability is unavailable through both the loaded MCP surface and the project-local CLI.
It still verifies the requested running behavior and does not claim completion from installation, Metro, or static checks alone.
